title: Exponential of the trace series is the inverse reverse characteristic polynomial
statement:
Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] of characteristic zero, so that $K$ is a $\mathbf Q$-algebra, let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], let $u:V\to V$ be a $K$-linear endomorphism, and let $T$ be an indeterminate. Let $P_u(T)=\det(1-Tu\mid V)\in K[T]$ be the reverse characteristic polynomial of $u$ [def-weil-reverse-characteristic-polynomial], regarded as a formal power series in $K[[T]]$ [def-weil-formal-power-series, def-weil-polynomial-as-power-series], and let $\operatorname{Tr}(u^n\mid V)\in K$ be the trace of the $n$-th iterate of $u$ [def-weil-endomorphism-trace]. Then, in $K[[T]]$,

$$
 P_u(T)\cdot\exp\Bigl(\sum_{n\geq1}\operatorname{Tr}(u^n\mid V)\frac{T^n}{n}\Bigr)=1,
$$

where $\exp$ is the formal exponential [def-weil-power-series-exponential] of the series $\sum_{n\geq1}\operatorname{Tr}(u^n\mid V)T^n/n$, which has constant coefficient $0$. Equivalently, $P_u(T)$ is a unit of $K[[T]]$ and $\exp\bigl(\sum_{n\geq1}\operatorname{Tr}(u^n\mid V)T^n/n\bigr)=P_u(T)^{-1}$; in logarithmic form, $\log\frac1{P_u(T)}=\sum_{n\geq1}\operatorname{Tr}(u^n\mid V)\frac{T^n}{n}$.

theorem inv_charpolyRev_eq_exp [CharZero K] (F : Module.End K V) :
    (F.charpolyRev : K⟦X⟧)⁻¹ =
      (PowerSeries.exp K).subst
        (PowerSeries.mk fun n ↦ if n = 0 then 0 else LinearMap.trace K V (F ^ n) / n)
lean.note: Existing exponential identity at DetTrace.lean:208, with the logarithmic identity at line 285. The shared context is a field K and a finite-dimensional K-vector space V; each theorem assumes CharZero K. The first states P inverse = exp(trace series). Since P has constant coefficient 1, it is a unit and multiplication gives P * exp(trace series) = 1. The second states logOf P = -traceSeries F, equivalently logOf(P inverse) = traceSeries F. No invertibility or semisimplicity of F is assumed.
